'''Hassan K. Khalil''' (born February 20, 1950, in [[Cairo]]) is an [[List of Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]] electrical engineer and University Distinguished Professor Emeritus at [[Michigan State University]]. He specializes in [[nonlinear control]] and singular [[perturbation theory]], and is widely known for his textbook ''Nonlinear Systems'', which received the 2002 [[International Federation of Automatic Control|IFAC]] Control Engineering Textbook Prize.<ref name="awards">{{cite web |title=Control Systems: An Introduction |url=https://www.amazon.com/Control-Systems-Introduction-Hassan-Khalil/dp/1607858266 |publisher=Amazon |access-date=26 December 2025}}</ref> He was named a [[Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) in 1989 for contributions to singular perturbation theory and its application to control.<ref name="IEEE">{{Cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37283039900|website=IEEE Xplore |access-date=8 July 2021|title=Hassan K. Khalil}}</ref>

==Education==
Khalil received his B.S. (1973) and M.S. (1975) degrees in electrical engineering from [[Cairo University]]. Moving to the United States for doctoral studies, he earned his Ph.D. (1978) from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] under the supervision of [[Petar V. Kokotovic]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=Khalil CV |url=https://www.egr.msu.edu/~khalil/resume_hassan.pdf |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Khalil joined Michigan State University as an assistant professor in 1978, the same year he completed his doctorate.<ref name="CV" /> Over his career at MSU, he advanced to become University Distinguished Professor in 2003, receiving multiple teaching honors along the way, including the Teacher Scholar Award (1983), the Withrow Distinguished Scholar Award (1994), the Distinguished Faculty Award (1995), and the Withrow Teaching Excellence Award (2020).<ref name="CV" /> Throughout his tenure, Khalil also consulted for [[General Motors]] and [[Delco Electronics]].<ref name="umich">{{cite web |title=Hassan K. Khalil biography |url=https://control.eecs.umich.edu/biokhalil.html |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=26 December 2025}}</ref>

A major focus of Khalil's research program at MSU has been the development of high-gain observers for nonlinear feedback control, a tool that originated at the university and has been advanced through the work of his 16 doctoral students and numerous postdoctoral researchers.<ref name="msu-research">{{cite web |title=Hassan Khalil Research |url=https://ece.msu.edu/researchfeature/hassan-khalil |publisher=Michigan State University |access-date=26 December 2025}}</ref> Khalil has published over 120 journal papers on singular perturbation methods and nonlinear control.<ref name="umich" />

In professional service, Khalil served as associate editor for the ''[[IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control]]'' (1984–1985), ''[[Automatica]]'' (1992–1999), and ''[[IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks|Neural Networks]]'' (1997–1998), and later as editor of ''Automatica'' for nonlinear systems and control (1999–2008).<ref name="Editorship">{{cite web |title=Hassan Khalil Biography|url=http://ieeecss.org/contact/hassan-khalil |website=IEEE Control Systems Society |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref> He was Program Chair of the 1988 [[American Control Conference]] and General Chair of the 1994 conference.<ref name="acc-history">{{cite web |title=ACC History |url=https://acc2025.a2c2.org/about/history |publisher=American Control Conference |access-date=26 December 2025}}</ref>

Khalil retired on May 15, 2020, and was granted emeritus status.<ref>{{cite web |title=Personal homepage of Hassan K. Khalil |url=https://www.egr.msu.edu/~khalil/ |website=MSU College of Engineering |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref>

==Books==
* ''Singular Perturbation Methods in Control: Analysis and Design'' (with [[Petar V. Kokotovic]] and John O'Reilly), Academic Press, 1986; reprinted by [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], 1999.
* ''Nonlinear Systems'', Macmillan, 1992; 2nd edition, Prentice Hall, 1996; 3rd edition, Prentice Hall, 2002, {{ISBN|0-13-067389-7}}.
* ''Nonlinear Control'', Pearson, 2015, {{ISBN|0-13-349926-X}}.
* ''High-Gain Observers in Nonlinear Feedback Control'', SIAM, 2017, {{ISBN|978-1-61197-485-0}}.
* ''Control Systems: An Introduction'', Michigan Publishing Services, 2024.

* {{cite journal |last1=Khalil |first1=H.K. |title=Adaptive output feedback control of nonlinear systems represented by input-output models |journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control |date=Feb 1996 |volume=41 |issue=2 |pages=177–188 |doi=10.1109/9.481517}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Seshagiri |first1=S. |last2=Khalil |first2=H.K. |title=Output feedback control of nonlinear systems using RBF neural networks |journal=IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks |date=Jan 2000 |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=69–79 |doi=10.1109/72.822511 |pmid=18249740}}

==Awards and honors==
* IEEE Fellow (1989), for contributions to singular perturbation theory and its application to control<ref name="IEEE"/>
* George S. Axelby Outstanding Paper Award, IEEE Control Systems Society (1989)<ref name="CV" />
* [[John R. Ragazzini Award|John R. Ragazzini Education Award]], [[American Automatic Control Council]] (2000)<ref name="CV" />
* IFAC Control Engineering Textbook Prize (2002)<ref name="awards"/>
* O. Hugo Schuck Best Paper Award, American Automatic Control Council (2004)<ref name="awards"/>
* [[International Federation of Automatic Control|IFAC]] Fellow (2007), for contributions to singular perturbation theory, nonlinear feedback control, and control education<ref name="CV" />
* Bode Lecture Prize, IEEE Control Systems Society (2015)<ref name="CV"/>
* [[Rufus Oldenburger Medal]], ASME (2025)<ref name="Oldenburger">{{cite news |last1=Mroczek |first1=Patricia |title=MSU’s Hassan Khalil receives national ASME medal for lifetime achievements |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2025/11/msus-hassan-khalil-receives-national-asme-medal-for-lifetime-achievements |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=Michigan State University |language=en}}</ref>
